name: Embedded OS & RTOS Security
description: Security assessment of embedded operating systems and real-time operating systems (RTOS) running on hardware targets. Covers privilege separation, memory protection unit (MPU/MMU) configuration, inter-process communication, task isolation, secure storage, and OS-level attack surfaces specific to embedded platforms (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, VxWorks, QNX, embedded Linux).

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to embedded OS or RTOS security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands embedded OS architectures and their security models
evidence: Can describe differences between bare-metal, RTOS, and embedded Linux environments
Understands MPU/MMU role in memory protection for embedded systems
Aware of common embedded OS attack surfaces (IPC, shared memory, privilege boundaries)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Assesses embedded OS configurations and identifies basic weaknesses under supervision
evidence: Analyzes embedded Linux build configurations for security settings (SELinux, seccomp, kernel hardening)
Identifies task privilege levels and MPU configuration in RTOS firmware
Tests for common misconfigurations (world-readable credentials, unprotected IPC) with guidance
Documents findings following lab reporting templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses embedded OS security across diverse platforms
evidence: Performs comprehensive security review of RTOS task isolation and privilege separation
Identifies and exploits embedded OS vulnerabilities (privilege escalation, memory corruption)
Assesses secure storage implementations and TEE integration on embedded platforms
Completed embedded OS assessments on 3+ different RTOS/embedded Linux platforms

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex embedded OS targets; develops assessment tooling; mentors team
evidence: Assesses proprietary or undocumented RTOS implementations through reverse engineering
Develops custom fuzzing harnesses for embedded OS components
Exploits complex vulnerability chains across privilege boundaries in embedded systems
Mentors team on embedded OS assessment techniques and platform-specific nuances

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on embedded OS security; publishes research; defines methodology
evidence: Published vulnerability research or CVEs against embedded OS platforms
Defines the lab's embedded OS assessment methodology and training program
Provides expert consultation to vendors on embedded OS hardening
Develops novel exploitation techniques for embedded OS security boundaries

assessment_methods.description: Assess the security configuration and attack surface of a target device running an RTOS or embedded Linux, producing a prioritized findings report
Present an unfamiliar embedded OS target and assess the analyst's approach to identifying the OS, mapping the attack surface, and identifying vulnerabilities
